item.title: T&T Seeks Stronger Trade Links With Martinique, Guadeloupe, French Guiana - TTT News

item.description: Serious concerns are mounting over idle resources inside the Couva Children’s Hospital, even as operations continue on a phased basis. item.title: Beyond The Report – Inside The Couva Children’s Hospital - TTT News
item.description: Serious questions are once again being raised about the Couva Children’s Hospital—more than a decade after it was built. Our reporter, Nicole Dookie, was granted exclusive access inside the facility and shared her experience with Virmala.

item.title: New Pharmacy Board Leadership - TTT News
item.description: New Pharmacy Board President Sanjay Mohammed joins Virmala on set to share his vision to strengthen the sector and address long-standing challenges.

item.title: T&T Urologist Wins Prestigious Urology Award - TTT News
item.description: A Trinidad and Tobago urologist has made history on the international stage, earning the prestigious Joint Surgical Colleges Medal—awarded to the candidate who achieves the highest score in the FRCS Urology Section 2 examination. Watch as Virmala chats with Acting Consultant Urologist at the POS General Hospital, Director of the North West Doctors Association and Medical Director of Tricare Medical Center, Dr Sharaz Mohammed.

item.title: 2026 Easter International Cycling Grand Prix - TTT News
item.description: President of the Trinidad and Tobago Cycling Federation, Rowena Williams joins Virmala on set to discuss the upcoming Easter International Cycling Grand Prix.

item.title: Redefining Normal – Cerebral Palsy Awareness Month - TTT News
item.description: Shamla examines the details of Cerebral Palsy with Neurologist Dr. Nicholas Maraj. Take a look as they explore the realities, challenges, and triumphs of life of persons living with CP.

item.title: Yellow Fever Case Confirmed In Monkey - TTT News
item.description: The Ministry of Health advises that, through laboratory testing, Yellow Fever has been confirmed in a deceased Red Howler monkey. It is important to note that there are no cases in humans. Yellow Fever is a viral disease transmitted by infected mosquitoes, including the Aedes aegypti.
